title: Per-endpoint ensemble quality marketplace and staged regional fallback protocol
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a pragmatic, per-endpoint SLO/SLI and error-budget policy that treats model ensembles (primary model + cheaper fallbacks) as a tradable quality currency. Deliver a staged regional fallback protocol and load-shedding rules that consume the ensemble quality marketplace to keep requests served under severe capacity pressure while preserving user-facing quality guarantees.

Scope:
- Formal SLI definitions for: success (semantic fidelity), latency (p50/p95/p99), and tail-quality regressions measured by promptset-based fidelity checks per endpoint and per model variant.
- An ensemble-quality accounting model where each variant has a quality score and a cost multiplier; requests may be served by cheaper variants when budget permits with controlled quality deltas.
- Error-budget consumption and replenishment rules tied to both latency and fidelity SLI breaches.
- Staged regional fallback choreography: local fallback -> cross-region reroute -> degraded-quality variant -> graceful reject.
- Circuit breaker triggers and hysteresis to avoid oscillation when toggling between variants or regions.
- Telemetry and dashboards to show ensemble-quality balance, per-endpoint SLI burn-rate, and rollback triggers.

Why this is different: Current SLO work at Redwood focuses on per-endpoint latency and availability; we lack a cross-variant, quality-aware accounting mechanism that can be used during capacity events to make principled tradeoffs between cost, latency, and output quality. This ticket operationalizes that marketplace and embeds it into failover and load-shedding logic.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLO/SLI schema (JSON spec) for endpoint-level fidelity, latency, and availability is documented and approved by SRE and Applied ML.
A quality score model for supported variants (numeric 0-100) exists and is stored in the model catalog; scores for at least three production variants are populated.
A deterministic error-budget calculator that factors fidelity breaches and latency violations is implemented and exposed via API.

A staged fallback controller is implemented with the following ordered actions: local cheap-variant substitution, region failover, fall back to degraded-mode with explicit quality tag, finally soft-reject. Controller supports per-endpoint policy knobs.
Circuit breaker rules (tripping thresholds and cooldown) are implemented with test coverage and integration tests against the runtime in the canary environment.
Dashboards showing ensemble-quality balance, per-endpoint burn rate, and a playbook runbook are published in the Console and referenced in the runbook.
Canary rollout to 10% traffic for low-risk endpoints and a rollback plan validated through injection tests is completed.
Runbook updated with playbook actions, escalation contacts, and post-incident remediation checklist.
notes: Trade-offs: more fine-grained quality accounting increases runtime decision complexity but reduces unnecessary rejections. We favor deterministic scoring over ML-based on-the-fly scoring for reliability and auditability.
Quality score derivation: start with promptset eval A/B comparisons to production baseline; normalize scores to 0-100 with documented rubric.
Edge-case: stateful chat sessions with KV cache must prefer variants that can honor session KV formats; policy should include a variant compatibility flag.
Fallback safety: when substituting variants, attach metadata to responses so clients can opt into degraded-mode handling (warning header, structured output field).
comments: 2025-01-10 Anika Patel: Initial triage — sketched the ensemble-quality marketplace model and listed required telemetry. Assigned to Evan to prototype controller decision path.

2025-01-12 Evan Ross: Spiked a controller prototype that consults the catalog and computes a candidate variant set. Observed increased API latency due to extra catalog lookup; planning to cache variant scores in the runtime node.
2025-01-14 Marco Delgado (Applied ML): Reviewed quality score rubric; requested adding a signal for hallucination-prone prompts and suggested a lower bound score for production substitution.
2025-01-15 Design review notes: Need UX artifact for Console to expose per-endpoint 'quality budget' and explain consumer-visible flags. DES-215 will cover the Console wireframes.

2025-01-16 SRE review: Proposed tripping rule: composite burn-rate > 1.5x sustained for 5m or 2x spike at p99 latency. Added requirement for circuit hysteresis of at least 3 min and exponential backoff.
2025-01-17 Evan Ross: Implemented RSI cache for variant scores (TTL 60s). Opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4826. Adding integration tests next.

2025-01-18 QA: began integration tests in canary cluster; observed a small mismatch between telemetry and reported burn because fidelity checks run asynchronously — will add synchronous probe sampling during canary.
Follow-ups: Add customer-facing doc summarizing degraded-mode semantics and how to detect/handle quality-tagged responses. PM to coordinate communications.
